title: Navigating the Growing Prospects and Growing Pains of Managed Aquifer Recharge
The Essential but Often Misunderstood Role of Economics in Groundwater Sustainability Research
abstract: To promote better groundwater policymaking, hydrologists and economists need to work together. The importance of hydrology is self-evident, but we posit that questions about the causes of and potential solutions for groundwater problems, and pathways to better policymaking, are fundamentally economics questions in that they rely on understanding people’s preferences, incentives, and responses to laws and other institutions that guide people’s actions. Not surprisingly then, most hydrologic research questions implicitly arise in response to economic demands and constraints. Hydrology and economics both rely on positive science involving theory, empirical methods, calibration, and validation. Indeed, their models can be linked to characterize and understand their interdependent dynamics. While other natural and social sciences also have important roles to play, this paper focuses primarily on how economics connects (ground)water to policymaking. Economics is a broad discipline with a primary role in understanding how people live in a landscape. Analogous to hydrology’s primary role in describing how water flows, recedes, seeps, evaporates, or recharges aquifers, economics describes people’s endeavors including their use of water, land, and other resources to produce, consume, trade, invest, conserve, and degrade the systems where they live. Policymaking is normative: it involves value judgments when assessing tradeoffs, setting priorities, or choosing among policy options. Economics is unique among disciplines in that it also comprises ‘normative analysis’ frameworks for measuring people’s values as a guide toward satisfying those preferences to the greatest extent possible (e.g. using benefit-cost analysis). But when natural science research is conducted without recognizing the economic considerations relevant to policymakers and managers, it may overlook critical ways that human system structures, dynamics, and people’s values inform the most promising ways to turn science into policy. By collaborating with economists, interdisciplinary research can bring natural sciences together with positive and normative economics to promote better groundwater policy.
abstract_zh: 为促进更好的地下水政策制定，水文学家与经济学家需要携手合作。水文学的重要性不言而喻，但我们认为，地下水问题的成因与潜在解决方案，以及通向更好政策制定的路径，本质上都是经济学问题，因为它们依赖于对人们的偏好、激励以及人们对法律和其他制度所作出反应的理解，而这些法律和制度指导着人们的行为。因此，大多数水文研究问题都隐含地源于经济需求与约束，这并不令人意外。水文学和经济学都依赖于包含理论、实证方法、校准和验证的实证科学。事实上，两者的模型可以相互连接，以刻画和理解其相互依存的动态。虽然其他自然科学与社会科学也具有重要作用，但本文主要关注经济学如何将（地下）水与政策制定联系起来。经济学是一门广博的学科，其首要作用在于理解人们如何在一片土地上生活。正如水文学的首要作用在于描述水如何流动、退去、渗漏、蒸发或补给含水层，经济学则描述人们的各种活动，包括他们利用水、土地和其他资源进行生产、消费、交易、投资、保护以及破坏其所居住的系统。政策制定具有规范性：在权衡取舍、设定优先次序或在政策选项之间进行选择时，它涉及价值判断。经济学在各学科中独具一格，因为它还包含“规范分析”框架，用于衡量人们的价值，以指导尽可能最大程度地满足这些偏好（例如，使用成本效益分析）。但是，如果自然科学研究在开展时未认识到与政策制定者和管理者相关的经济考量，它可能会忽略人类系统结构、动态以及人们的价值观如何影响将科学转化为政策的最有前景方式的关键路径。通过与经济学家合作，跨学科研究能够将自然科学与实证及规范经济学结合起来，从而推动更好的地下水政策。

title: Designing Water Markets for Climate Change Adaptation
The Dynamic Impacts of Pricing Groundwater
venue: Journal of the Association of Environmental and Resource Economists
abstract: This paper evaluates own-price dynamics in taxing environmental externalities. We exploit a natural experiment that exposed some firms to a large and persistent price increase for groundwater, a setting characterized by incomplete markets. Using five years of post-treatment data on farm-level water use, we find that water conservation doubles between the first and fifth year of the tax. Failure to account for dynamics in policies designed to manage groundwater will mischaracterize the price elasticity of demand and introduce efficiency costs.
abstract_zh: 本文评估了对环境外部性征税中的自身价格动态效应。我们利用一项自然实验，该实验使部分企业面临地下水价格大幅且持续上涨，而这一情境的特点是市场不完全。利用五年征税后的农场层面用水数据，我们发现，水资源节约量在征税第一年与第五年之间翻了一番。若在旨在管理地下水的政策中忽视动态效应，将会错误刻画需求的价格弹性，并带来效率损失。

title: Recharge Net Metering (ReNeM) is a Novel, Cost-effective Management Strategy to Incentivize Groundwater Recharge
abstract: Managed aquifer recharge, which uses available water to augment groundwater resources, holds promise as a strategy to reduce chronic groundwater overdraft. However, water management agencies often confront hurdles when implementing managed aquifer recharge. Favourable sites for recharging water are often located on private land, and common-pool resource conflicts frequently disincentivize voluntary private participation. We introduce recharge net metering (ReNeM), a conceptually novel, market-based mechanism to help overcome these barriers and achieve multiple extractive and non-extractive benefits from improved groundwater management. ReNeM enables an agency to incentivize practices that enhance infiltration and groundwater recharge. Here we formalize the basis for incentivizing recharge and conduct a multi-party cost–benefit analysis of an operating ReNeM programme in California’s Pajaro Valley. Calculations show that water supply from ReNeM can be achieved at a lower cost than many viable alternatives and can produce multiple benefits for collaborating entities and stakeholders.
abstract_zh: 人工补给含水层（managed aquifer recharge）利用可用水源来补充地下水资源，有望成为减少慢性地下水超采的一种策略。然而，水资源管理机构在实施人工补给时往往面临诸多障碍。适宜补水的地点通常位于私人土地上，而公共池塘资源冲突经常削弱私人自愿参与的积极性。我们提出了补给净计量（recharge net metering，ReNeM），这是一种概念上新颖的、基于市场的机制，旨在帮助克服这些障碍，并通过改善地下水管理实现多重开采性与非开采性效益。ReNeM使管理机构能够激励那些能够增强下渗与地下水补给的做法。在此，我们阐明了激励补给的理论基础，并对加利福尼亚州帕哈罗谷一项正在运行的ReNeM计划开展了多方成本效益分析。测算结果表明，ReNeM所提供的供水成本低于许多可行的替代方案，并能够为合作主体及利益相关方带来多重效益。

title: The Political Economy of Groundwater Management: Descriptive Evidence from California
venue: American Agriculture, Water Resources, and Climate Change, National Bureau of Economic Research

title: Untapped Potential: Leak Reduction is the Most Cost-Effective Urban Water Management Tool
abstract: Providing sufficient, safe, and reliable drinking water is a growing challenge as water supplies become more scarce and uncertain. Meanwhile, water utilities in the United States lose approximately 17% of their delivered water to leaks each year. Using data from over 800 utilities across four U.S. states, California, Georgia, Tennessee, and Texas, we characterize the heterogeneity in water losses across the U.S., develop a model to assess the economically efficient level of losses, and use this model to compare the net benefits of several proposed water loss regulations and modeling approaches. Combining economic and engineering principles, our model shows that for the median utility, it is economically efficient to reduce water losses by 34.7%, or 100 acre-feet (AF) per year. The median cost of water savings from leak management is $277/AF, which falls well below the cost of traditional water management tools. However, the optimal level of water losses strongly depends on utility-specific characteristics, leading to large differences in the potential for cost-effective leak reduction across utilities. We show that water loss management can lead to water savings that generate net economic benefits, but only if management approaches incorporate economic and engineering principles.
abstract_zh: 随着水资源日益稀缺且不确定，提供充足、安全和可靠的饮用水正成为一项日益严峻的挑战。与此同时，美国的供水公司每年因漏损而损失的供水量约占其供水总量的17%。利用来自加利福尼亚州、佐治亚州、田纳西州和得克萨斯州四个美国州的800多家供水公司的数据，我们刻画了美国各地水损失的异质性，构建了一个评估经济效率意义上最优漏损水平的模型，并利用该模型比较了若干拟议的水损失监管措施和建模方法的净效益。结合经济学与工程学原理，我们的模型表明，对于中位数供水公司而言，将水损失减少34.7%（即每年100英亩英尺，AF）在经济上是有效率的。漏损管理带来的节水成本中位数为每英亩英尺277美元，远低于传统水资源管理工具的成本。然而，最优漏损水平在很大程度上取决于各供水公司的特征，这导致不同公司在具有成本效益的漏损削减潜力上存在巨大差异。我们表明，水损失管理可以带来产生净经济效益的节水效果，但前提是管理方法必须融合经济学与工程学原理。

title: Missing Markets: Evidence on Agricultural Water Demand from Volumetric Pricing
Using Price Elasticities of Water Demand to Inform Policy
abstract: This survey distills recent work on the price elasticity of demand for urban and agricultural water and outlines how it can inform the design of market-based approaches to manage increasingly scarce water resources. We offer a brief description of the water sector, including the primary users, main water sources, and market failures in the allocation and use of surface water and groundwater. A review of recent empirical research on the price elasticities of agricultural and urban water demand shows the progress made in our understanding of user response to prices and reveals substantial heterogeneity in the price response. We apply what we have learned about elasticities to surface water markets and price-based groundwater management. Heterogeneity in price elasticities suggests that water transfers may lead to large efficiency gains, but that their magnitude is site specific. Groundwater pricing may cost-effectively manage groundwater and fund the development of alternative water supplies, but heterogeneity in elasticity estimates highlights that the conservation and revenue generated are basin specific.
abstract_zh: 本综述梳理了近期关于城市和农业用水需求价格弹性的研究成果，并阐述了这些成果如何为设计以市场为基础的方法、管理日益稀缺的水资源提供依据。我们简要介绍了水务部门，包括主要用水者、主要水源以及地表水和地下水在配置与使用中的市场失灵问题。对近期农业与城市用水价格弹性实证研究的回顾表明，我们在理解用水者对价格的反应方面已取得进展，并揭示出价格反应存在显著的异质性。我们将所了解到的弹性知识应用于地表水市场和基于价格的地下水管理。价格弹性的异质性表明，水权转让可能带来巨大的效率收益，但其规模因地而异。地下水定价或许能以成本效益较高的方式管理地下水，并为替代供水的开发提供资金，但弹性估计值的异质性表明，节水效果与所产生的收入具有明显的流域特异性。

title: Compound Natural and Human Disasters: Managing Drought and COVID-19 to Sustain Global Agriculture and Food Sectors
Cost Effectiveness of Livestock Guardian Dogs for Predator Control
The Gains from Agricultural Groundwater Trade and the Potential for Market Power: Theory and Application
abstract: This article models and estimates the efficiency gains from using market‐based instruments relative to command and control to manage groundwater. A theoretical model of an imperfectly competitive groundwater market is developed to show how the magnitude and distribution of the gains from trade change as market structure varies. Market structure is a key consideration because future groundwater markets will likely feature geographic limitations to trade, large agricultural players, and a legal environment that is conducive to forming cartel‐like coalitions. Application of the model to a groundwater‐dependent agricultural region in southern California shows the existence of large gains from trade, despite the potential for market power, with benefits up to 36% greater than that under command and control. Distributional impacts, however, can be sizable even for small degrees of market power. Simulations that vary market conditions show that results likely generalize to other groundwater basins.
abstract_zh: 本文对采用市场化工具相对于命令与控制型手段管理地下水所带来的效率收益进行了建模和估计。我们构建了一个不完全竞争地下水市场的理论模型，以展示随着市场结构变化，贸易收益的规模与分配如何变化。市场结构是一个关键考量，因为未来的地下水市场很可能存在地域上的贸易限制、大型农业参与者，以及有利于形成卡特尔式联盟的法律环境。将该模型应用于加利福尼亚州南部一个依赖地下水的农业地区，结果表明，尽管存在市场势力的可能性，贸易收益依然巨大，其收益比命令与控制型管理下高出最多36%。然而，即使市场势力程度很小，分配影响也可能相当可观。改变市场条件的模拟表明，这些结果很可能可推广至其他地下水流域。

title: Using Cost-Benefit Analysis to Understand Adoption of Winter Cover Cropping in California’s Specialty Crop Systems
abstract: Winter cover crops could contribute to more sustainable agricultural production and increase resiliency to climate change; however, their adoption remains low in California. This paper seeks to understand barriers to winter cover crop adoption by monetizing their long-term economic and agronomic impacts on farm profitability in two of California's specialty crop systems: processing tomatoes and almonds. Our modeling effort provides a present, discounted valuation of the long-term use of winter cover crops through a cost-benefit analysis. A net present value model estimates the cumulative economic value of this practice. We then explore how the long-term trade-offs associated with winter cover crops can affect an operation's profits under a spectrum of hypothetical changes in California's agricultural landscape. Our analysis sheds light on the barriers to adoption by reporting benefit-cost ratios that indicate profitability across several scenarios; however, benefits and costs accrue differently over time and with long planning horizons. At the same time, a small portion of gained benefits are external to the grower. Findings from this study reveal that winter cover crops in California can be profitable in the long-term, but the extent of profit depends on the cropping system, extent of irrigation savings due to improved soil function, access to financial subsidies and climate change. Winter cover crops can return positive net benefits to growers who have flexible contractual obligations, can wait for the long-term return on investment and manage cover crops as closely as cash crops. This analysis contributes to the study of conservation agriculture practices by explaining possible reasons for low adoption through an economic valuation of the implications of soil management choices and policy counterfactuals.
abstract_zh: 冬季覆盖作物有助于实现更可持续的农业生产，并增强对气候变化的适应能力；然而，在加利福尼亚州，其采用率仍然很低。本文试图通过将冬季覆盖作物对农场盈利能力的长期经济与农学影响货币化，来理解其采用的障碍，研究对象为加州两类专业作物系统：加工番茄和杏仁。我们的建模工作通过成本—收益分析，对长期使用冬季覆盖作物给出了折现后的现值估值。净现值模型估算了该做法的累计经济价值。随后，我们探讨了在加州农业景观出现一系列假设性变化的情况下，与冬季覆盖作物相关的长期权衡如何影响经营者的利润。我们的分析通过报告在多种情景下均表明盈利的收益—成本比，揭示了采用障碍；然而，收益与成本随时间的分布不同，且在较长的规划期限下表现各异。与此同时，所获收益中有一小部分对种植者而言属于外部收益。本研究发现，加州的冬季覆盖作物可以实现长期盈利，但利润的大小取决于种植制度、因土壤功能改善而节省的灌溉量、财政补贴的获取途径以及气候变化。冬季覆盖作物能够为合同义务灵活、能够等待长期投资回报、并像管理经济作物一样精细管理覆盖作物的种植者带来正的净收益。本分析通过对土壤管理选择及政策反事实情形的经济估值，解释了采用率低的可能原因，从而为保护性农业实践的研究作出了贡献。
